title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page states a standard theorem from a course-style exposition (Thm 1, followed on the next page by Thm 2, existence of Eπ, and the Borel construction). Setup: π is a discrete group and E → B is a principal π-covering. For any space X there is a map h_X : [X,B] → H^1(X,π), sending the homotopy class of f : X → B to the isomorphism class of the pulled-back covering f*E. Here H^1(X,π) is defined as the set of isomorphism classes of principal π-coverings of X. This map is natural in X. The theorem says two conditions are equivalent: (1) h is an isomorphism of functors, i.e. h_X is bijective for every X; in that case (E,B,π) is called a universal π-covering and B a classifying space Bπ. (2) E is contractile (contractible). This is the classical characterization of K(π,1) = Bπ as the base of a contractible principal π-bundle. The page serves as background for the next page: the Borel construction Eπ ×_π X and the exact sequence relating π_1(X), the equivariant fundamental group π_1(X,π), π and π_0(X), with π_2(Bπ) = 0. The cote title ('Théorie de Kummer ?') and the next page suggest equivariant or orbifold fundamental groups, plausibly in a teaching or anabelian-adjacent context around 1980. This page itself is purely textbook material.
errors: As stated, 'pour tout espace X' is too general. Two things need hypotheses: homotopy invariance of pullbacks, and the identification of [X,B] with coverings. The usual hypotheses are X a CW complex (or paracompact, or locally path-connected and semi-locally simply connected) and B of the homotopy type of a CW complex.
For general B, condition 1) corresponds to E being weakly contractible. Genuine contractibility follows only when E has CW homotopy type.

hot(X,B) must mean free (unbased) homotopy classes so that it matches unbased isomorphism classes of coverings. For connected X both sides are then Hom(π_1X,π)/conjugation. This is implicit but correct.

ideas.what: Classification of principal π-coverings by homotopy classes of maps to a base with contractible total space
ideas.modern_name: Classifying space Bπ = K(π,1); universal principal bundle Eπ → Bπ
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook material (Steenrod, Husemoller). Grothendieck treats torsors and H^1 in Tôhoku and SGA but not this exact topological statement.

ideas.what: Defining H^1(X,π) as isomorphism classes of π-torsors (non-abelian H^1)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'A general theory of fibre spaces with structure sheaf' (Kansas 1955); Tôhoku; Giraud, Cohomologie non abélienne
